messages.subject: Part 2 vs Part 5 output
parts:
Hello, 

I am using the following code to find the time spent in various physical activity zones:
PA_algorithm <- "vanHees2015"
GGIR::GGIR(datadir= "/Users/vaishnavicherukupalli/REASA/reasa/input",
           outputdir= "/Users/vaishnavicherukupalli/REASA/reasa/Output",
           minimum_WW_length.part5 = 10,
           minimum_MM_length.part5 = 10,
           includedaycrit = 10,
           dofirstpage =FALSE,
           do.parallel = FALSE,
           strategy = 1,
           excludefirstlast.part5 = FALSE,
           do.enmo = TRUE,
           ignorenonwear= TRUE ,
           acc.metric = "ENMO",
           do.visual= TRUE,
           threshold.lig = c(44.8),
           threshold.mod = c(100.6),
           threshold.vig = c(428.8),
           data_masking_strategy = 5,
           maxdur = 4,
           Nvaliddays= 4,
           HASIB.algo = PA_algorithm
)
However, I am having trouble with the number of valid days in the output. In my part 2 summary, the number of days with valid hours is greater than number of valid days in part 5 summary, which is causing loss of analysis power.  I am unsure as to why this is happening and this is Warning R is generating:

Warning message:
In breaks_i[bi] <- fullQqq[grep(breaks[bi], ts$time[fullQqq])] :
  number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length

I will really appreciate if you can help me out with this. Thank you!

messages.author: 4b9dc262ec278dc5
messages.subject: Re: Part 2 vs Part 5 output
parts:
Hi,

In part 2, GGIR uses includedaycrit to define valid days, which requires a minimum number of hours per calendar day.

In part 5, GGIR uses includedaycrit.part5, which only looks at the number of valid hours during the awake time classified in that specific day. 

Also, the timewindow definition in part 5 ("MM", "WW", "OO") can make the number of valid days inconsistent between parts 2 and 5.

Best,
Jairo
